issue.title: tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk.py selected-tribe fold level 1 exceeds its 40 ms key-to-paint p95 budget on athena
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-l6 (epic land phase), found while running phase `immediate`'s named-but-skipped verification (`pytest -s -m slow tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk.py`).

REPRODUCTION: at master HEAD d1e88155b, `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -m slow tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk.py::test_bench_selected_tribe_jk_at_each_fold_level` fails on selected-tribe fold level 1, 3/3 runs:
  run 1: next p95 48.4 ms / p50 29.8; prev p95 55.5 / p50 29.7
  run 2: next p95 48.9 / p50 31.9; prev p95 50.1 / p50 30.6
  run 3: next p95 49.2 / p50 28.1; prev p95 46.7 / p50 31.5
against `_SELECTED_TRIBE_P95_BUDGET_MS = 40.0`. The other four scenarios in the file pass, including test_bench_agents_jk_and_panel_navigation (the ordinary Agents-tab row j/k gate at the 16 ms budget).

NOT CAUSED BY EPIC sase-l6: reverting the epic's `immediate` phase commit ffa63b5ed (the only phase that changed what the cheap/pre-debounce paint renders) produces statistically identical numbers, 2/2 runs: next p95 53.1 / prev p95 46.5, and next p95 49.8 / prev p95 46.2. The epic's other phases do not touch the tribe-panel render path at all.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH INVESTIGATING RATHER THAN JUST RE-BASELINING: this is not the outlier-p95-over-a-low-median shape that sase-dx described. The *median* is 28-34 ms, i.e. 70-85% of a p95 budget, so half of all measured tribe hops already cost about two 60 Hz frames.

CONFOUND TO RULE OUT FIRST: the measuring host was loaded (load average ~18 on 64 cores, several `yes` processes pinned at 99% CPU, a concurrent Rust build earlier in the session). Re-measure on a quiet athena before concluding there is a real regression. If the numbers hold on an idle host, bisect for a real key-to-paint regression in selected-tribe panel cycling; the budget and the scenario were introduced together by d3cf6236e (perf(tui): streamline selected tribe navigation, sase-6z.6) and the budget's own comment justifies 40 ms as 'two 60 Hz frames' for a two-region panel-chrome repaint.

SCOPE: decide real-regression vs host-sensitivity with an idle-host measurement; if real, find and fix the regression without weakening the user-visible budget; if host-sensitivity, make the measurement robust the way sase-dx wanted for the Artifacts scenario rather than raising the number.

All six are sase-l6 land-phase follow-ups on a path the epic already fixed with process-wide revalidating snapshot caches: store pruning/rotation, moving the artifact-file index into Rust indexed storage, scoping show_empty()'s cache clear, cold-cache re-measurement, auditing non-TUI read_artifact_file_index callers, and one bench budget (bench_tui_jk selected-tribe fold level 1, ~48 ms vs a 40 ms p95 budget on a 64-core host at loadavg ~30). No independent reporters, no user-visible defect. The one resolver kept open from this cluster is sase-lw, which measured 400-800 ms per TUI selection with no cache at all. Store growth stays visible: ~/.sase/artifacts/index.jsonl is 7.8 MB today -- re-file with a +1 and a fresh figure if it starts costing real latency.

evidence.note:
Independently reproduced 13 days later at master a7b702863, and the confound this bead
asked to rule out first turns out not to be dischargeable.

REPRODUCTION (2026-08-27, athena, `pytest -s -m slow tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk.py -k
selected_tribe`), selected-tribe fold level 1 against `_SELECTED_TRIBE_P95_BUDGET_MS = 40.0`:

  full-file run: next p50 34.33 / p95 55.12 / max 324.98; prev p50 32.54 / p95 54.57 / max 329.73
  solo run 1:    next p50 32.87 / p95 50.66 / max  52.50; prev p50 34.11 / p95 61.20 / max 257.09
  solo run 2:    next p50 29.38 / p95 54.52 / max 236.03; prev p50 32.56 / p95 51.08 / max 234.46

That is the same non-outlier shape this bead recorded (p50 28-34 ms then, 29-34 ms now):
the median alone is 73-85% of the whole p95 budget, so half of all tribe hops still cost
about two 60 Hz frames. 3/3 runs fail, matching the original 3/3.

THE "RE-MEASURE ON A QUIET ATHENA" CONFOUND IS NOT DISCHARGEABLE AS WRITTEN. The original
report attributed load average ~18 on 64 cores to `yes` processes and a concurrent Rust
build. Today athena sits at load average 18.21 / 17.68 / 20.56 with no such session
running: the top consumers are routine `sase_chop_*` workers plus `sase` itself. Load ~18
on 64 cores (~28% utilization) is this host's ordinary resting state, not an artifact of
the measuring session, so "wait for a quiet athena" is not a step a future agent can
actually complete. Either the bench must tolerate athena as it normally runs, or the
budget has to be justified against a pinned-CPU environment.

A REMEDIATION THAT IS NOW VALIDATED IN THIS EXACT FILE. Epic sase-ug added a sibling
bench (`test_bench_agents_jk_with_and_without_the_link_rail`) and hit the same
instability, so the fix was worked out there and measured:

  - two sequential arms at n=20, p95 compared directly: delta spread -2.7 .. +7.2 ms,
    failing 2 of 8 runs on an unchanged tree;
  - four alternating short arms pooled to n=48 per direction: delta spread -2.8 .. +2.9 ms,
    passing 8 of 8.

Two effects drive that. First, at n=20 the p95 index is the 2nd-highest sample, so one
~250 ms scheduler stall moves it; at n=48 the index sits 2 samples below the top, so the
stall lands in `max` and leaves p95 alone. Second, this host's absolute j/k p50 drifts
between 12 ms and 20 ms across runs as background load changes; two measurements taken at
two different times sample that drift, while alternating short rounds let it fall on both.

`test_bench_axe_jk`, `test_bench_clan_jk_at_each_panel_fold_level`, and this scenario
would all keep their current user-visible budgets under that pooling -- it makes the
measurement robust without weakening the budget, which is what bead:sase-dx asked for.
Note the distinction this bead already drew still holds: axe and clan are the
outlier-p95-over-low-median shape (re-run alone, axe passes and clan reads p95 16.26 vs a
16.0 budget over a p50 of 11.29), whereas selected-tribe fails on its median.

Reported by the land agent for epic sase-ug while verifying that epic's own new bench in
this file. Not caused by sase-ug: this bead predates the epic, the numbers are unchanged,
and the epic's rail composes last (just above the footer) and is `display = False` until
an index has chips, so it occupies no layout row on the tribe path.
